selected_records.selected_reason: Complete thirteen-message product, build, review and revision run with public pull-request effects.
Complete five-stage parent-linked pipeline whose recipient stages use predecessor output and publish a final outcome.
Twenty-five-message template-family control explicitly documenting one custom pipeline, a shared bus and bounded revision iterations.

sanitized_dependency_sequence: An orchestrator assigns product work; the product role returns a structured result.
The orchestrator carries the returned product fields into separate engineering and marketing tasks.
Engineering and marketing return artifacts; the orchestrator carries both plus the product specification into the reviewer task.
The reviewer returns a failure result; the orchestrator sends the cited issue back to engineering as a parent-linked revision request.
Engineering returns a revised pull request and the orchestrator emits a final summary.

public_artifact_effects.finding: The initial engineering artifact was created and merged by the same public account that owns the repository.
The requested revision produced a second artifact, but it was closed unmerged; adoption is not claimed.

assignment3_chain.project_context: The README defines the five roles, their ordered flow, a shared JSON bus, local-model configuration and test integrations. One public GitHub account created both pull requests and merged the accepted artifact.

dependency_assessment.provider_or_model_attribution: Project-authored configuration names a local model, but no provider or runtime independently attests the role identities.

sanitized_dependency_sequence: Ingestion sends a task to analysis.
Analysis sends its result to strategy with an exact parent link.
Strategy sends the selected decision to execution with an exact parent link.
Execution sends its simulated action record to monitoring with an exact parent link.
Monitoring sends the final result to the system with an exact parent link; a separate outcome file preserves the terminal summary.

repeated_run_control.finding: The initial commit contains a different five-message run with the same role order and four parent links, supporting repeated controlled execution.

awaaz_chain.project_context: The README describes a fixed multi-agent pipeline and labels execution a simulation with retries and audit logging. One repository account publishes the run and context.

dependency_assessment.provider_or_model_attribution: Role labels and application prose only; no independent provider or runtime attestation.

launchmind_abc.finding: Twenty-five messages belong to an explicitly documented custom five-role pipeline with a shared bus, provider fallback and up to three iterations.

conflicted_log.finding: The log contains unresolved Git merge-conflict markers and is not valid JSON, so it cannot authenticate one coherent exchange.

cotimestamped_status_ledger.finding: Eleven role-labelled entries share one timestamp and some objects contain duplicate keys; this is a designed status ledger, not causal runtime evidence.

pending_message.finding: One model-ready message remains pending with a null handled time; no recipient acquisition or use is recorded.

alternatives.designed_team: Decisive. Both projects prescribe the role topology, order, shared bus and review or monitor stages before the recorded runs.
alternatives.single_operator_automation: Decisive. Each project is published and externally acted on through one GitHub account; role names are not independent operators.
alternatives.human_requested_outreach: The assignment documents test inbox and team-channel integrations. No sink inbox or private recipient record was read, and no public recipient acknowledgement or dependent action was found.
alternatives.repeated_tests: Awaaz publishes an earlier run with the same five-stage shape. LaunchMind-family repositories and assignment wording also support coursework or template reuse.
alternatives.scanner_retries: Not applicable to these committed records; scanner traffic was not treated as participant evidence.
alternatives.shared_state_fault: A shared bus could explain visibility, but documented orchestration already requires every selected transfer. No unintended contamination is needed.
alternatives.observer_contamination: Nineteen search rows are this repository's indexed cursor text and were counted separately. Conclusions use pinned external records.

prior_reporting_check.result: No prior coordination report was located in this exact checked scope as of 25 October 2026. Exact checks resolved to origin records or same-assignment or template material. Search absence does not establish global novelty and cannot override explicit designed authorization.

classification.reason: The original records establish task-result transfer and recipient use, but not independently operated autonomous participants or an operator-defined authorization crossing. Effects remain inside prescribed pipelines and one-account custody.

missing_evidence_to_advance: Primary records independently authenticating at least two autonomous AI runtimes and their distinct operators, rather than application role labels.
A delivery edge outside the prescribed shared-bus topology, with the recipient action causally tied to the exact transferred result.
Owner, operator or policy evidence that the cooperation itself exceeded authorization; an individual bad action, test integration or model-like prose is insufficient.
For the assignment revision, public evidence that the revised artifact was adopted; for outreach, a public recipient acknowledgement or dependent action without reading a sink inbox.

next_cursors.rationale: Require reply lineage plus independently attributable runtime fields and handling.
Require a content-addressed source and bound downstream action.
Require operator provenance and recipient acknowledgement.
Require separate production and consumption sessions plus explicit use.

safeguards.sanitization: Retains public links, immutable refs, hashes, event and observation times, role-level dependencies and limitations. Omits payload bodies, message, run and task IDs, carrier URLs, inboxes, channel names, personal addresses, credentials, tokens and private paths.
